issue.title: get_blind_signatures_for_quote returns non-deterministic order
issue.body:
When a wallet checks a completed melt quote via GET /v1/melt/quote/bolt11/{id}, the change field contains BlindSignatures loaded from the blind_signature table without an ORDER BY clause. 

Also, it seems like maybe  `get_melt_request_and_blinded_messages` in quotes.rs fetches the unsigned blinded messages from DB during saga recovery (mint crash/restart). These B_ values are then zipped with denomination amounts and signed. If they come back out of order, the mint assigns the wrong denomination to the wrong B_, producing mismatched signatures at the source. This means even the POST response can have wrong pairings after a saga recovery.

The overall issue that when reading from the db the ordering of outputs is not guaranteed and wallets expect the outputs to be in the same order as the blinded messages sent to the mint

issue.title: Wallet handle receive when offline

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Currently, receiving in the CDK wallet requires the wallet to be online to perform a swap. However, Cashu enables offline receiving pending DLEQ verification and locking conditions. We should add this capability to CDK.

One way to implement this is by adding a new function to the wallet that accepts a token and specific conditions. These conditions would include the minimum locktime, a list of mints, and whether the token must be locked. The CDK wallet would then verify the token's DLEQ proof and ensure these conditions are met. Upon verification, it would add the proofs to the database in a new state, `PendingReceive`, and add them to the wallet's transaction list. Wallets should display these transactions with a warning indicating that they must be swapped for final settlement.

Since the proofs are not truly received until they are swapped, we would also need a function that checks for all pending receives and executes the swaps.

issue.title: feat(cdk-axum): support redis-cluster for caching
issue.body:
closes #1578 
### Description

This PR adds support for Redis Cluster and Valkey Cluster to the cdk-axum HTTP caching backend.

Currently, the cache only supports a single-node Redis connection, which fails in clustered environments because it cannot handle "MOVED" redirections. This change introduces a cluster-aware client that automatically routes requests to the correct nodes and handles cluster topology changes.

-----
### Key Changes 
1.Introduced RedisClient enum to support both Standard and Cluster connection types.
2. Added cluster and cluster-async features to the redis dependency.
3. Updated HttpCacheRedis to use the appropriate connection methods for both single-node and cluster setups.
4. Added support for cluster configuration via environment variables:
            CDK_MINTD_CACHE_REDIS_USE_CLUSTER: Enable cluster mode. 
            CDK_MINTD_CACHE_REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES: Comma-separated list of node URLs.

-------
### Notes to the reviewers

1. The Config struct in redis.rs was updated to make connection_string optional, as cluster users will use cluster_nodes instead. Backward compatibility is maintained for existing single-node setups.
2 . The HttpCache::from(config) logic in mod.rs now intelligently selects the client type based on the provided configuration.
3. Added specific error logging for cluster-specific failures to aid in debugging distributed environments.

The current call paths invoke `fetch_from_http` with either `Some(client), None` from `load_from_mint` or `None, Some(auth_client)` from `load_auth`, so this clears `active_keysets` globally and then only repopulates it for the path that was called. issue.title: fix: replace blocking Condvar pool with async Semaphore
issue.body:

Under the default pool size of 1, concurrent requests can block all Tokio worker threads, deadlocking the runtime the task holding the connection can never be scheduled to release it. Replace with tokio::sync::Semaphore so waiters yield to the async runtime instead of blocking.

I know my ai flagged: 

## Summary
I reviewed PR #1808 in `cashubtc/cdk`. The PR refactors database connection pooling logic inside `cdk-sql-common/src/pool.rs` by switching from threading primitives (`Condvar`) to asynchronous Rust semantics using `tokio::sync::Semaphore`. In doing so, it introduces a vulnerability: the `get_timeout` function, which is supposed to wait asynchronously up to a configured `timeout` duration for an available connection, completely ignores the `timeout` parameter during semaphore acquisition (`self.semaphore.clone().acquire_owned().await`). Under load or exhaustion, this causes the task to block indefinitely rather than returning the expected `Error::Timeout`. This breaks the system's ability to gracefully degrade or fail fast when limits are hit, leading to resource exhaustion, starvation of other dependent tasks, and potential deadlocks in production environments, making this a high-severity DoS vulnerability introduced by this PR.

I think there were some other things last time I asked my agent to review it as well.

issue.title: Migrate INTEGER/BIGINT columns storing u64 values to TEXT
issue.body:
### Description

Cashu amounts are u64, but neither SQLite nor PostgreSQL has an unsigned 64-bit integer type. Both INTEGER and BIGINT are signed, so values above `i64::MAX` silently overflow when cast to i64. This PR stores all amount-like columns as TEXT instead, eliminating the risk of truncation entirely.

Once columns become TEXT, PostgreSQL refuses to do arithmetic on them; expressions like total_issued + EXCLUDED.total_issued simply fail. Even with SQLite, casting large text values back to integers for math is unreliable. Rather than patching the SQL with ever more complex `CAST/COALESCE` chains, this PR moves all arithmetic into Rust. Each keyset amounts update now reads the current value, adds the delta with checked_add (which returns an explicit error on overflow instead of wrapping silently), and writes the result back. The same applies to SUM() aggregations — amounts are fetched as individual rows and summed in Rust.

A secondary fix handles PostgreSQL's `::` cast syntax (`column::TYPE`), which the SQL parser was misinterpreting as a named bind parameter.

As a next step, amounts should be streamed from storage rather than loaded as full result sets into memory, and all math should be performed in the mint or wallet, outside the storage layer.

This PR depends on #1957 and #1808

+//! Keyset amounts helper — reads current values and performs math in Rust
+
+use cdk_common::database::Error;
+use cdk_common::Id;
+
+use crate::database::DatabaseExecutor;
+use crate::stmt::query;
+use crate::{column_as_number, unpack_into};
+
+/// Current totals for a single keyset, as stored in the `keyset_amounts` table.
+struct KeysetAmounts {
+    total_issued: u64,
+    total_redeemed: u64,
+    fee_collected: u64,
+}
+
+/// Fetches the current `keyset_amounts` row for the given keyset, returning
+/// `None` if no row exists yet.
+async fn get_keyset_amounts<C>(conn: &C, keyset_id: &Id) -> Result<Option<KeysetAmounts>, Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    let row = query(
+        r#"SELECT total_issued, total_redeemed, fee_collected FROM keyset_amounts WHERE keyset_id = :keyset_id"#,
+    )?
+    .bind("keyset_id", keyset_id.to_string())
+    .fetch_one(conn)
+    .await?;
+
+    match row {
+        Some(row) => {
+            unpack_into!(let (total_issued, total_redeemed, fee_collected) = row);
+            Ok(Some(KeysetAmounts {
+                total_issued: column_as_number!(total_issued),
+                total_redeemed: column_as_number!(total_redeemed),
+                fee_collected: column_as_number!(fee_collected),
+            }))
+        }
+        None => Ok(None),
+    }
+}
+
+/// Builds an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert query that only overwrites the
+/// specified column, leaving the others at their INSERT defaults.
+fn upsert_query(column: &str) -> String {
+    format!(
+        r#"
+        INSERT INTO keyset_amounts (keyset_id, total_issued, total_redeemed, fee_collected)
+        VALUES (:keyset_id, :total_issued, :total_redeemed, :fee_collected)
+        ON CONFLICT (keyset_id)
+        DO UPDATE SET {column} = :{column}
+        "#
+    )
+}
+
+/// Writes the given amounts back to `keyset_amounts`, inserting or updating
+/// the target column.
+async fn upsert_keyset_amounts<C>(
+    conn: &C,
+    keyset_id: &Id,
+    amounts: &KeysetAmounts,
+    column: &str,
+) -> Result<(), Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    query(&upsert_query(column))?
+        .bind("keyset_id", keyset_id.to_string())
+        .bind("total_issued", amounts.total_issued)
+        .bind("total_redeemed", amounts.total_redeemed)
+        .bind("fee_collected", amounts.fee_collected)
+        .execute(conn)
+        .await?;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// Adds `delta` to `total_issued` for the given keyset.
+///
+/// Reads the current value from the database, performs the addition in Rust
+/// with overflow checking, and writes the result back.
+pub(crate) async fn increment_total_issued<C>(
+    conn: &C,
+    keyset_id: &Id,
+    delta: u64,
+) -> Result<(), Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    let mut amounts = get_keyset_amounts(conn, keyset_id)
+        .await?
+        .unwrap_or(KeysetAmounts {
+            total_issued: 0,
+            total_redeemed: 0,
+            fee_collected: 0,
+        });
